sections: 356.2.b and 356.4: optional additional costs and their discounts
416: ready as a state versus a Ready action
358.3.a: prevented movement does not make a choosing spell illegal

implementation_contract: Crescent Guardian has a conditional optional additional cost, not the Accelerate keyword. Its controller must already have played a spell that turn. A spell need not resolve successfully to count. A paid extra Chaos Power changes its entry to ready.

Use the existing finalized spell-play history for the condition; choosing or starting payment alone must not count. Preserve cost selection and legality across previews, pending payment, free plays and rollback.
Discounts can reduce a declared optional additional cost to zero without removing its benefit. Do not grant Accelerate-specific metadata to Crescent Guardian.

Entrenched Boar offers an optional entry replacement, not an additional cost or a response-window trigger. Accepting makes that physical unit enter ready and unable to Move for the rest of that turn. Declining preserves other entry-ready effects without imposing this restriction.

The Boar restriction applies to standard and effect Moves, expires at turn end, and does not carry to a newly played physical object. Corrective Recall is distinct from Move. Effects choosing a movement-restricted unit may still be legal; negate only the prohibited Move.
Entering ready does not itself perform a Ready action. Expose accurate choice labels and restriction reasons to the native UI, API, AI and both companion levels.
